title: Fit Response Surface Model
action: Fit a second-order polynomial regression model to the experimental tensile strength data using the FSP parameters (number of tool passes, rotational speed, transverse speed) as predictor variables, including all linear, quadratic, and interaction terms. Use ordinary least squares. Save the fitted model coefficients as evidence.
description: Fitted regression coefficients for the quadratic response surface model.
output_schema: A JSON object containing the intercept and coefficient values for terms: A, B, C, A2, B2, C2, AB, AC, BC. Example keys: {"intercept": ..., "A": ..., "B": ..., ...}

title: Optimize FSP Parameters for Maximum Tensile Strength
action: Using the fitted quadratic model, determine the parameter combination (tool passes as integer in {1,2,3}, rotational speed in [800,1000] rpm, transverse speed in [15,25] mm/min) that maximizes predicted tensile strength. Write the optimal parameters and the predicted tensile strength to optimum_parameters.json.
description: Optimal FSP parameter values and the corresponding predicted maximum tensile strength.

title: Compute Model Comparison Metrics
action: Using the predicted tensile strength from the previous step and the provided experimental confirmation tensile strength (162.89 MPa) and base material tensile strength (135 MPa), compute deviation_percentage = (predicted_tensile_strength - 162.89) / predicted_tensile_strength * 100, and improvement_percentage = (162.89 - 135) / 135 * 100. Write the results to model_comparison.json.
description: Metrics comparing model prediction to experimental data and base material.
